chunks: Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn 'Isa, from Isma'il ibn Sa'd al-Ash'ari, said:
I asked him about a garment of silk: may men perform salat (prayer) in it? He said: "No."
And the hadith that we presented earlier, from the narration of Muhammad ibn Ahmad ibn Yahya, from Muhammad ibn 'Abd al-Jabbar, also indicates what we have said.

key_terms.الثَّوْبِ: the garment or piece of clothing being asked about in the ruling
key_terms.الرِّجَالُ: men; the category to whom this ruling applies
key_terms.الْإِبْرِيسَمِ: silk; the material whose use in salat (prayer) by men is being discussed
key_terms.الْحَدِيثُ: hadith; the report cited as supporting proof
key_terms.رِوَايَةِ: narration; a transmitted report used as evidence

ai.seo_question: Can men perform salat (prayer) while wearing silk clothing according to this hadith?
ai.summary: This hadith gives a legal ruling that men may not perform salat (prayer) while wearing a silk garment. The closing statement notes that an earlier narration also supports this ruling, reinforcing the jurisprudential basis of the prohibition.
